prompt.context_jp: 「ヤダ！ ママ___いないなら 生きてる意味なんてない」
prompt.prompt_jp: ママ___いないなら 生きてる意味なんてない
prompt.prompt_en: Young Mai is crying out that life is meaningless without her mom. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: In a 〜がいない conditional like this, が marks the existence/absence of the subject as the key new condition. The focus is on the specific fact that mom isn't here — not on contrasting her with someone else.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn 'mom' into an established topic and sound more detached/contrastive, which clashes with Mai's desperate outburst. も ('also') makes no sense here.

contrast_examples.jp: ママがいないと寂しい。
contrast_examples.en: It's lonely when mom isn't here. (focus on her absence)

contrast_examples.jp: ママはいないけど、パパはいるよ。
contrast_examples.en: Mom isn't here, but dad is. (contrastive は)

prompt.context_jp: ママ___ずっと ずっと 会いたかったのは 今の万理華だよ
prompt.prompt_jp: ママ___ずっと ずっと 会いたかったのは 今の万理華だよ
prompt.prompt_en: The mother is telling her daughter who she really wanted to see. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: In a 〜のは〜だ cleft, the subject inside the relative clause (ママ) is marked with が. The focus of the whole sentence is on 今の万理華 — who it is the mother wanted to see.
feedback.incorrect_en: を would need a transitive verb pattern that isn't present; 会いたい takes に for the person. に alone wouldn't mark ママ as the one doing the wanting.

contrast_examples.jp: 私が好きなのはあなただよ。
contrast_examples.en: The one I like is you. (が inside relative, cleft focus)

contrast_examples.jp: 私はあなたが好きだよ。
contrast_examples.en: I like you. (plain topic–comment)

prompt.context_jp: 万理華___何も悪くないの 万理華___そのまんまでいいの
prompt.prompt_jp: 万理華___何も悪くないの
prompt.prompt_en: The mother reassures Marika directly. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: Marika is the established topic of this emotional reassurance. は presents her as the known subject and lets the comment ('isn't to blame at all') land as the message.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would sound like it's identifying who is innocent out of several candidates — too clinical for a tearful apology. も would mean 'Marika too', which isn't the point.

contrast_examples.en: Marika isn't to blame. (topic–comment reassurance)

contrast_examples.jp: 万理華が悪いんじゃない、私が悪いの。
contrast_examples.en: It's not Marika who's at fault — it's me. (exhaustive が, contrast)

prompt.context_jp: もう お昼の時間よ おなかに何か入れないと ご飯___元気のもとなんだから
prompt.prompt_jp: ご飯___元気のもとなんだから
prompt.prompt_en: Takie is making a general claim about food. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: This is a generic statement ('Food is the source of energy'). は marks ご飯 as the topic about which a general truth is being asserted.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it sound like 'it's food (not something else) that's the source of energy' — an exhaustive-listing reading that doesn't match her gentle encouragement. を can't mark the subject.

contrast_examples.en: Dogs are faithful animals. (generic topic は)

contrast_examples.jp: 元気のもとが何かって？ご飯が元気のもとよ。
contrast_examples.en: What's the source of energy? Food is. (exhaustive が in reply)

prompt.context_jp: 声___届かないって 切ないわね
prompt.prompt_jp: 声___届かないって 切ないわね
prompt.prompt_en: The fortune-teller comments on the ghosts' predicament. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: Inside the quoted 'situation' clause 声が届かない, が marks the subject of a neutral event-description. The whole 〜って clause is the new idea being commented on.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn 声 into a contrastive topic ('voices, as for them, don't reach…'), which weakens the direct description. を doesn't fit an intransitive 届く.

contrast_examples.en: The phone isn't getting through. (plain event)

contrast_examples.jp: 声は届くけど、気持ちは届かない。
contrast_examples.en: The voice reaches, but the feelings don't. (contrastive は)

prompt.context_jp: 宇田くんってさ 私のこと嫌いだよね
prompt.prompt_jp: 宇田くん___私のこと嫌いだよね
prompt.prompt_en: Moriya confronts Uda directly. Which particle most naturally substitutes for ってさ as a plain topic marker?

feedback.correct_en: She's picking Uda out as the topic she wants to comment on: 'As for you, you dislike me, don't you?' は fits that topic–comment frame.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark him as the newly-identified disliker, as if answering 'who dislikes me?' — too abrupt here. を would mark him as a direct object, which doesn't fit.

contrast_examples.jp: 宇田くんは私のこと嫌いだよね。
contrast_examples.en: You dislike me, don't you, Uda. (topic)

contrast_examples.jp: 宇田くんが私のこと嫌いなの？
contrast_examples.en: Is it Uda who dislikes me? (identifying が)

prompt.context_jp: これからは なくしたものじゃなく ママ___くれたものを見つめて 生きていかないか？
prompt.prompt_jp: ママ___くれたものを見つめて
prompt.prompt_en: Keisuke is urging Mai to look at what Mom gave them. Which particle fits inside the relative clause?

feedback.correct_en: Inside a noun-modifying clause (ママ〜くれたもの), the subject takes が, not は. は is generally not used for the subject of a relative clause.
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside a relative clause would sound ungrammatical or imply a contrast scoping outside the clause. を would double-mark an object and clash with くれる.

contrast_examples.en: I read the book Mom gave me. (が inside relative)
Mom (topic) gave me that book. (main-clause は)

prompt.context_jp: 父は弁当箱の包み___ 机の縁にそっと置いた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 父は弁当箱の包み___ 机の縁にそっと置いた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the lunchbox package here?

feedback.correct_en: 置く takes を for the thing being placed. The topic is 父 (marked by は), and 弁当箱の包み is the direct object he sets down.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make the package a subject, but it isn't doing anything. に marks the destination (机の縁に), not the moved object.

contrast_examples.en: I put the book on the desk. (を = thing placed)
There's a book on the desk. (が = subject of state)

prompt.context_jp: 会社への帰り道、圭介___ある陶芸教室の前___足を止めた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 圭介はある陶芸教室の前___足を止めた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks where Keisuke stopped?

feedback.correct_en: 足を止める is an action happening at a location, so the place takes で. The pottery studio's front is where the action occurs.
feedback.incorrect_en: に would mark a destination/arrival point rather than the site of a dynamic action. を would make the place a path being traversed.

contrast_examples.jp: 店の前で立ち止まった。
contrast_examples.en: I stopped in front of the shop. (で = site of action)
I arrived in front of the shop. (に = destination)

prompt.context_jp: 少女はそっと手を伸ばし、母の頬___触れた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 母の頬___触れた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for the thing being touched?

feedback.correct_en: 触れる takes に for the point of contact. Her hand reaches out and makes contact at the mother's cheek.
feedback.incorrect_en: を is used with 触る in some patterns but with 触れる the standard partner is に. で would mark means, not target.

contrast_examples.en: Words that touch the heart. (に = point of contact)
I stroked the cheek. (撫でる takes を)

prompt.context_jp: 父は顔をしかめたまま、牛乳を一気に呷った。「うわっ… ママの味___程遠いな」
prompt.prompt_jp: ママの味___程遠いな
prompt.prompt_en: Keisuke compares his cooking to Mom's. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: 程遠い is used with に for the standard being distant from. The stacked は after に adds a contrastive nuance ('as for matching Mom's flavor, it's far off').
feedback.incorrect_en: がは is not a valid combination. では would mean 'in Mom's flavor' which doesn't match 程遠い's expected pattern.

contrast_examples.en: Far from ideal. (に required by 程遠い)

contrast_examples.jp: 完成にはまだ時間がかかる。
contrast_examples.en: It'll still take time to complete. (には = contrast on goal)

prompt.context_jp: 失ったもの___見つめて 死ぬまで過ごすの？
prompt.prompt_jp: 失ったもの___見つめて
prompt.prompt_en: Takie's remembered voice urges Keisuke. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: 見つめる is a transitive verb — the thing being gazed at is marked with を. 'What you lost' is the direct object of his staring.
feedback.incorrect_en: に with 見つめる is non-standard here. が would make it the subject, which doesn't match the verb's structure.

contrast_examples.en: To stare at the sky. (を)
To be trapped by the past. (に with passive-flavored verb)

prompt.context_jp: 友利 私___ ちゃんと知ってるわよ あんたが やればできる子だって
prompt.prompt_jp: 私___ ちゃんと知ってるわよ
prompt.prompt_en: Takie reassures Tomori. Which particle fits for 私?

feedback.correct_en: She's setting herself up as the topic — 'As for me, I know it well' — with a subtle contrastive feel ('others may not, but I do'). は fits perfectly.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it 'it's me who knows' — more identifying/exhaustive than this gentle reassurance. も ('also') wouldn't match the implied contrast.

contrast_examples.jp: 私はあなたを信じてる。
contrast_examples.en: I believe in you. (topic/contrast)

contrast_examples.jp: 私があなたを信じてる。
contrast_examples.en: I'm the one who believes in you. (identifying)

prompt.context_jp: ママが亡くなった10年前___ お父さん こうやって 麻衣と話さなきゃいけなかったんだ
prompt.prompt_jp: ママが亡くなった10年前___
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle attaches to the time expression here?

feedback.correct_en: A specific point in time ('ten years ago, when Mom died') takes に to anchor when the action should have happened.
feedback.incorrect_en: で here would feel like duration/means and doesn't suit a point-in-time anchor. を doesn't mark time points.

contrast_examples.en: I got up at 7. (に = time point)
I finished it in a week. (で = span)

prompt.context_jp: 翌朝、少女はゆっくりと___を開いた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 少女はゆっくりと___を開いた
prompt.prompt_en: Which word fits — the girl slowly opens her ___?

feedback.correct_en: 目を開く is the set collocation for waking up and opening one's eyes. The context ('next morning, slowly') fits waking.
feedback.incorrect_en: 耳を開く isn't a common collocation; 耳を澄ます ('strain one's ears') is standard. 口を開く means 'to start speaking' — possible in other contexts but not consistent with 'the next morning, slowly'.

contrast_examples.jp: 目を開けて起き上がった。
contrast_examples.en: She opened her eyes and sat up.
She quietly opened her mouth (started to speak).

prompt.context_jp: ママが なってほしい万理華は あの子なんだって だから もう うちに___のは やめにしようって
prompt.prompt_jp: うちに___のは やめにしようって
prompt.prompt_en: Marika's inner voice says she gave up trying to ___ home. Which verb fits?

feedback.correct_en: うちに帰る ('to go home') is the natural collocation when the speaker returns to her own household. The context is Takie-inside-Marika deciding to stop trying to return to her own family.
feedback.incorrect_en: 戻す is transitive ('put something back'), not 'go back'. 入る ('enter') lacks the sense of returning home.

contrast_examples.en: I want to go home soon.
Put the book back in its place.

prompt.context_jp: 嫌いなのは 全然かまわないけど 仕事中に そういう ___ 冗談 やめてくれないかな
prompt.prompt_jp: そういう ___ 冗談 やめてくれないかな
prompt.prompt_en: Moriya calls Uda's joke what kind of joke?

feedback.correct_en: くだらない冗談 ('stupid/pointless joke') is a very common collocation and matches Moriya's irritated tone toward Uda's harassment.
feedback.incorrect_en: うれしい冗談 and すばらしい冗談 would be positive — the opposite of what she means. She's rebuking him, not praising him.

contrast_examples.jp: くだらないことで悩まないで。
contrast_examples.en: Don't worry about trivial things.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼のジョークはいつも面白い。
contrast_examples.en: His jokes are always funny.

prompt.context_jp: あんたたち 相手にしてると キリがないから とっとと___しなさい
prompt.prompt_jp: とっとと___しなさい
prompt.prompt_en: The fortune-teller tells the ghosts to hurry up and do what?

feedback.correct_en: 成仏する means 'to pass on / ascend to the next life' — exactly what she wants the lingering spirits to do.
feedback.incorrect_en: 出発 (depart) and 予約 (reservation) don't fit the context of spirits that need to move on from this world.

contrast_examples.jp: 早く成仏してください。
contrast_examples.en: Please pass on quickly.
I'll depart tomorrow morning.

prompt.context_jp: 別部署の同期が 自分飛び越えて上司って ___でしょ 普通
prompt.prompt_jp: 別部署の同期が 自分飛び越えて上司って ___でしょ 普通
prompt.prompt_en: Uda vents about being passed over. Which verb captures 'to feel bitter/let-down' here?

feedback.correct_en: 腐る literally 'to rot', is a colloquial way to say 'to feel discouraged/sulk' when things don't go your way. It matches Uda's bitter mood.
feedback.incorrect_en: 喜ぶ ('be happy') and 笑う ('laugh') are the opposite — being passed over doesn't make you laugh.

contrast_examples.en: Don't get down about something like that.
To rejoice at the news of passing.

prompt.context_jp: あの… ___を 上げさせてもらっても いいですか？
prompt.prompt_jp: ___を 上げさせてもらっても いいですか？
prompt.prompt_en: Aikawa visits the Niijima home. What does he ask to offer at the altar?

feedback.correct_en: 線香を上げる ('to offer incense') is the standard set phrase for paying respects at a Buddhist altar, which is what Aikawa is doing for Mai's late mother.
feedback.incorrect_en: 花火 (fireworks) and お茶 (tea) don't fit the ritual. 線香 is specifically what you offer at a 仏壇.

contrast_examples.jp: お線香を上げに伺います。
contrast_examples.en: I'll come by to offer incense.
I'll make some tea.

prompt.context_jp: ごめん しばらく ___になりたい
prompt.prompt_jp: しばらく ___になりたい
prompt.prompt_en: Mai asks to be left alone. Which word fits?

feedback.correct_en: ひとりになりたい ('I want to be alone') is the natural idiom and fits Mai's withdrawn mood after her mother's second disappearance.
feedback.incorrect_en: 元気になりたい means 'I want to feel better' — not matching her request to push Aikawa away. 大人になりたい ('want to be an adult') is unrelated.

contrast_examples.jp: 少しひとりになりたい。
contrast_examples.en: I want to be alone for a bit.
Get well soon.

prompt.context_jp: 守屋さんに___のは ちょっとカッコ悪くないか？
prompt.prompt_jp: 守屋さんに___のは ちょっとカッコ悪くないか？
prompt.prompt_en: Keisuke scolds Uda for taking out his frustration on Moriya. Which verb fits?

feedback.correct_en: 人に当たる means 'to vent frustration on someone / lash out at someone'. That's exactly what Uda has been doing to Moriya.
feedback.incorrect_en: 勝つ ('win') doesn't fit this interpersonal context. 尋ねる means 'ask' — not negative behavior.

contrast_examples.jp: 家族に八つ当たりしないで。
contrast_examples.en: Don't take it out on your family.
I beat my rival.

prompt.context_jp: お父さん もう二度と 麻衣のこと___から
prompt.prompt_jp: もう二度と 麻衣のこと___から
prompt.prompt_en: Keisuke vows never to do what to Mai again?

feedback.correct_en: 投げ出す means 'to abandon / give up on'. He's promising he will never again abandon his parental responsibility to Mai, echoing his earlier confession.
feedback.incorrect_en: 思い出さない ('won't remember') is the opposite of a father's promise. 受け取らない ('won't receive') doesn't fit this context.

contrast_examples.jp: 途中で仕事を投げ出した。
contrast_examples.en: He abandoned the job halfway through.

contrast_examples.jp: 昔のことを思い出した。
contrast_examples.en: I remembered the old days.

prompt.context_jp: Mai asks Aikawa to leave her alone.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural for Mai's tired, pained request to be left alone?

choices.text: しばらく ひとりになりたい
しばらく ひとりになることを希望します
しばらく ひとりになるべきだ

feedback.correct_en: The 〜になりたい form is natural, personal, and emotionally direct — exactly what Mai says in the scene.
feedback.incorrect_en: Option B is overly formal/stiff Japanese that nobody would say to a close classmate. Option C ('I should be alone') sounds like a judgment, not a request.

contrast_examples.jp: ちょっとひとりにしてほしい。
contrast_examples.en: I want to be left alone for a bit.

contrast_examples.jp: ひとりになることを希望いたします。
contrast_examples.en: I hereby wish to be alone. (bizarrely formal)

prompt.context_jp: Keisuke invites Uda to lunch to patch things up.
prompt.prompt_en: Which invitation sounds most natural for a senior colleague inviting a younger colleague to lunch?

choices.text: 宇田くん よかったら ランチ行きませんか？
宇田くん ランチに行くことを命じます
宇田くん ランチを食べろ

feedback.correct_en: よかったら〜ませんか is a soft, polite invitation that respects the listener's choice — ideal for repairing a workplace relationship.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is an absurd order from a corporate manual. C is a blunt command that would make the tension worse.

contrast_examples.jp: よかったら、お茶でもどうですか？
contrast_examples.en: If you'd like, how about some tea? (soft invite)
Come here right now. (command)

prompt.context_jp: Takie urges Keisuke to eat lunch.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing most naturally expresses 'you should put something in your stomach'?

choices.text: おなかに何か入れないと
おなかで何か入れないと
おなかを何か入れないと

feedback.correct_en: おなかに入れる uses に to mark the destination of the food — the standard collocation.
feedback.incorrect_en: で (means/location of action) and を (direct object) don't fit the 'put X into Y' pattern needed here.

contrast_examples.en: Put something in your mouth. (に = destination)
Put a book in the bag. (に = destination)

prompt.context_jp: The girl, waking up, wonders aloud whether what she experienced was a dream.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural for a sleepy child musing to herself?

choices.text: 私… 夢を見てたのかな？
私… 夢を観察していたのでしょうか？
私… 夢の目撃者でしたか？

feedback.correct_en: 夢を見る is the standard idiom for 'to have a dream', and 〜かな softly voices self-wonder — exactly what a sleepy child would say.
feedback.incorrect_en: B uses 観察 ('observe') which sounds scientific, not childlike. C treats dreaming as witnessing an event — very unnatural phrasing.

contrast_examples.en: I had a strange dream.
An experiment that observes dreams. (clinical)

prompt.context_jp: Keisuke tries to tell Mai they should look forward, not back.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing most naturally captures 'let's look at what Mom gave us, not what we lost'?

choices.text: なくしたものじゃなく ママがくれたものを見つめて 生きていかないか？
なくしたものじゃなく ママがくれたものを見つめで 生きていかないか？
なくしたものじゃなく ママはくれたものを見つめて 生きていかないか？

feedback.correct_en: The て-form 見つめて and が inside the relative clause (ママがくれた) are both correct. The line matches the natural rhythm of a tender fatherly appeal.
feedback.incorrect_en: Option B uses 見つめで, which is a wrong conjugation. Option C puts は inside a relative clause, which Japanese generally doesn't allow for the subject of the relative — it should be が.

contrast_examples.jp: 母がくれた言葉を忘れない。
contrast_examples.en: I won't forget the words Mom gave me.
Mom gave me words. (main-clause topic)
